subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-agent plugin installation in core before per-agent plugin runtime activation, discovery precedence, and uninstall/security semantics are designed end to end?
rationale: This is not only CLI plumbing: plugin install records determine code execution, trusted source handling, allowlists, discovery precedence, and agent isolation, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Hold for end-to-end scoped contract
options.body: Require install, runtime discovery/activation, update, uninstall, validation, docs, and security tests to agree before exposing `--agent`.

options.title: Narrow to internal helpers
options.body: Remove the public flag for now and land only maintainer-approved internal record helpers if they are useful for the next design step.

options.title: Return to the canonical issue
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep the design discussion on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97749 until the product and security boundary is settled.

recommendation.title: Hold for end-to-end scoped contract
recommendation.body: Require install, runtime discovery/activation, update, uninstall, validation, docs, and security tests to agree before exposing `--agent`.

likelyOwner.reason: The product/security contract intersects plugin install roots, command surfaces, and the multi-agent direction where this owner has adjacent history.
